deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a theoretical derivation. It is the reduction of a series of observations of an oscillating magnet or galvanometer needle read by telescope against a scale. The method is the one Gauss and Weber used in the 1830s. Weber's name appears on the previous page, which fits a dating to the Göttingen magnetic and galvanic work; the '1801' among the pen trials at the bottom does not date the page.

(a) Rest readings. The faint pencil column on the left opens with 618.8, 617.8, 618.0, the scale readings of the needle at rest.

(b) Turning points. The rest of the pencil column lists successive turning points (elongations) x_k of the swinging needle:
- before the first double line: 257.0, 706.1, 290.2, 724.0, 304.2, 732.9, 311.2, 738.0;
- between the double line and the next rule: 659.0, 748.5, 655.0, 739.2, 651.2, 736.1, 649.4;
- after the rule: 422.2 (the transcription reads 422.7), 657.8, 426.2, 660.8, 428.5, 661.7.

(c) Pair sums (my reconstruction, verified for every row). The first ink column is A_n = x_n + x_{n+1}, the sum of two consecutive elongations, i.e. twice the momentary centre of oscillation:
- A_0 = 257.0 + 706.1 = 963.1 and A_1 = 706.1 + 290.2 = 996.3, and so on up to A_6 = 311.2 + 738.0 = 1049.2;
- A_7 = 738.0 + 659.0 = 1397.0 and A_8 = 659.0 + 748.5 = 1407.5, and so on up to A_13 = 736.1 + 649.4 = 1385.5;
- A_14 = 649.4 + 422.2 = 1071.6 (struck out), A_15 = 422.2 + 657.8 = 1080.0, and so on up to A_19 = 428.5 + 661.7 = 1090.2;
- the entry indexed -1 uses the initial rest reading: 618.0 + 257.0 = 875.0.

(d) Deviations. The constant 1229.9 (alternatively 1229.8), written at the top, is taken as twice the undisturbed rest position, about 615. The second column is B_n = |1229.9 − A_n|, twice the displacement of the centre of oscillation from rest:
- n = −1 to 6 and n = 15 to 19: B_n = 1229.9 − A_n, so the centre lies below rest;
- n = 7 to 13: B_n = A_n − 1229.9, so the centre lies above rest.

The acting force was therefore reversed between the swings at 738.0 and 659.0, and again between 649.4 and 422.2, as with a commutator. The pair sums straddling a reversal (n = −1, 7, 14) mix two states and are meaningless. Gauss marked them: n = −1 with a dash, and 167.1 and 158.3 in parentheses, with 1071.6 struck out. Read across the reversals, |B| decreases monotonically: 266.8, 233.6, 215.7, 201.7, 192.8, 185.8, 180.7, 177.6, 173.6, 164.3, 160.5, 157.5, 155.7, 149.8, 145.8, 142.7, 140.6, 139.7. This describes a slowly decaying deflecting force (for example a weakening galvanic current, or an after-effect).

(e) Testing the decay law (right margin). Five-figure mantissas of the common logarithms of B at every sixth row:
- log 266.8 = 2.42619
- log 180.7 = 2.25696
- log 157.5 = 2.19728
- log 140.6 = 2.14799

Their successive differences are 16923, 5968 and 4929 (units of 10^-5). For a purely exponential decay these would be constant. They are not: the decrement shrinks strongly, so the decay is slower than geometric. It looks more like a fast transient on a slow decay, or decay toward a nonzero limit. The page is thus a check of whether the force decays geometrically.
errors: Row 17: 1229.9 − 1087.0 = 142.9, or 142.8 with the alternative constant 1229.8, but Gauss wrote 142.7, a slip of 0.1–0.2.
Rows 12, 13, 15 and 16 use 1229.8 while the other rows use 1229.9 (the two values at the top). This is an inconsistency of 0.1, not a real error.
The bracketed or struck entries at n = −1, 7, 14 are pair sums across a change of state. Gauss correctly treats them as invalid.
All other sums, differences, logarithms and log-differences check correctly.

results.what: Centre of oscillation of a swinging needle from the sum of consecutive turning points, with deflection measured from twice the rest position (reversed-force readings).
results.modern_name: Method of turning points (elongations) for the equilibrium position of a damped oscillator; commutator (reversal) method
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and Weber, Göttingen magnetic observations, 1832–1840

results.what: Test of exponential decay of the deflection by differencing common logarithms at equal intervals.
results.modern_name: Semi-log test for exponential decay / logarithmic decrement

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine reduction of experimental data in the Gauss–Weber manner: pair sums of elongations, reversal of the force, and a logarithmic test of decay. It is of documentary interest as raw laboratory data but contains no new mathematics.

checkable.asserts: Equals [1071.6, 1080.0, 1084.0, 1087.0, 1089.3, 1090.2] for n = 14..19, which requires the pencil reading 422.2.
= [16923, 5968, 4929], the log-differences, which are not constant, so the decay is not exponential.

transcription_corrections: Left pencil column: '422,7' should be 422.2, as required by 1080.0 = 422.2 + 657.8 and 1071.6 = 649.4 + 422.2.
The entry at index -1 is 354.9 (a struck 354 is overwritten), with a dash, i.e. rejected; it equals 1229.9 − (618.0 + 257.0).
Row 7 'A' is 1397,0 (= 738.0 + 659.0) and its B (167,1) is bracketed as invalid.
The right-margin numbers 42619, 25696, 19728, 14799 are log mantissas of 266.8, 180.7, 157.5, 140.6; 16923, 5968, 4929 are their differences.
